From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: Fwd: Request: Promo credit & trial extension — Olive Health POC

Thanks Grace — good summary. Accounting guidance below based on the facts provided.

Short answer: we should issue a credit memo that references INV-20270601 and post it to contra-revenue (promo allowance) rather than directly reversing revenue. That preserves an audit trail and keeps our revenue recognition intact.

Details / required items:
- Documentation required before finance can post: signed SOW (we have), explicit customer approval (email or DocuSign addendum), and HubSpot deal ID (OLV-1973).
- Credit memo form: please fill the Credit_Memo_Request_Form_OLV-1973.pdf (attached) and route to finance@redwood.com.
- GLA mapping: use Contra-Revenue: Promo Allowance GLA 4012. If legal classifies the credit as a direct sales discount, we may use GLA 4020 — we need confirmation from sales/legal.
- Tax: Since Olive Health is US-based and this is a promotional allowance tied to a service invoice, typically no separate sales tax adjustment is required, but verify if their state requires tax adjustments. If the tax on the original invoice needs a reduction, we will need the customer's tax jurisdiction and billing address; the credit memo must explicitly state tax amount reduction.
- Timing: Once we receive the completed form and customer approval, finance can draft the credit memo in ~3 business days and target posting within 7 business days.

Operational note: If the customer insists on a dollar-for-dollar invoice offset (netting the invoice), we still issue the credit memo and apply it to INV-20270601 in AR — that achieves the same effect but keeps the documentation consistent.

Please confirm whether the customer wants a full offset (recommended) or a partial/praorated credit and then I will queue the memo.

Marcus Lin
Director, Revenue Operations
marcus.lin@redwood.com
Finance — Redwood Inference
